screenSummary.playArea: The play area shows the electromagnetic spectrum as a bar from gamma rays (short wavelength) on the left to radio waves (long wavelength) on the right, a magnified strip of visible light, and an animated wave for each photon.
screenSummary.controlArea: The control area has readouts of each photon's wavelength, frequency and energy, a menu of everyday examples, checkboxes to compare two photons and to show the equations, and a Reset All button.
screenSummary.interactionHint: Move the spectrum marker with the arrow keys to change the wavelength and watch the frequency and energy change.

spectrum.currentDetails: Photon 1 is {{wavelength}}, in the {{region}} region: frequency {{frequency}} hertz, energy {{energy}} joules per photon, or {{molar}} kilojoules per mole.
spectrum.currentDetailsCompare: Photon 2 is {{wavelength}}, in the {{region}} region. Photon 2 has {{energyRatio}} times the energy of photon 1.
spectrum.markerHelp: Left is shorter wavelength and higher energy; right is longer wavelength and lower energy.

screenSummary.playArea: The play area shows a Bohr model of a hydrogen atom, its energy-level diagram, and a spectrum strip that records each line the atom emits or absorbs.
screenSummary.controlArea: The control area chooses emission or absorption, moves the electron between levels, sets and fires the lamp in absorption mode, chooses energy units, and shows the equations. A Reset All button is last.
screenSummary.interactionHint: In emission mode, move the electron to level 3, then to level 2, and listen for the photon it emits.

hydrogenAtom.currentDetails: The electron is in level {{n}}, with energy {{energy}}. {{lines}} lines recorded.
hydrogenAtom.currentDetailsIonized: The atom is ionized: the electron is free. {{lines}} lines recorded.
hydrogenAtom.emitted: The electron drops from level {{from}} to level {{to}} and emits a {{wavelength}} nanometre photon, {{color}}, in the {{series}} series.
hydrogenAtom.absorbed: A {{wavelength}} nanometre photon is absorbed. The electron jumps from level {{from}} to level {{to}}.
hydrogenAtom.excited: The discharge lifts the electron from level {{from}} to level {{to}}.
hydrogenAtom.passedThrough: The {{wavelength}} nanometre photon passes straight through: its energy matches no jump.
hydrogenAtom.ionizedEvent: The {{wavelength}} nanometre photon frees the electron. The atom is ionized.
hydrogenAtom.recaptured: The electron is recaptured into level 1.

screenSummary.playArea: The play area shows a light source, the coloured strip seen through the spectroscope, and a chart of intensity against wavelength from 380 to 780 nanometres.
screenSummary.controlArea: The control area chooses the light source and its gas, metal or temperature, a reference gas to compare with, and, for the mystery tube, checkboxes to name the gas. A Reset All button is last.
screenSummary.interactionHint: Choose a gas, then move the wavelength cursor along the chart with the arrow keys to read the wavelength of each bright line.

lineSpectra.currentDetails: Showing {{source}}. The brightest line is at {{peak}} nanometres. The cursor is at {{cursor}} nanometres, where the intensity is {{intensity}} percent.
lineSpectra.cursorHelp: Move along the spectrum to read wavelength and intensity.
